Hi team,

ShadowBridge sent back a narrow-read of our initial demarc diagram and a few questions surfaced around the control-plane reachability and egress expectations from their tenant runtime. I attached their initial reference and an annotated PNG they gave us.

Three asks to unblock engineering:
1) Confirm where their control-plane agents should initiate TLS connections (regionally vs. centralized control cluster).
2) Decide whether we require a dedicated egress NAT per tenant or a shared egress with per-tenant SNAT pools for auditability.
3) Agree on a canary handoff checklist (we need a minimal ops MOP to run the pilot).

I want to keep this tight — propose a short sync tomorrow (30m) to lock demarc and handoff items. If you can, please add inline notes on the PDF.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: ShadowBridge VPC alignment + control/data demarcation

Ethan — quick read and a few replies inline below. High level: we should treat control-plane signaling as regional (prefer lower RTT), but allow fallback to central control plane for failover. Concrete notes: see page 3 of the attached PDF for proposed port/TLS endpoints.

1) Control-plane initiation: prefer outbound TLS from tenant nodes to regional control endpoints (mutual TLS). We can avoid incoming firewall holes on the customer's side. Fallback: if regional endpoint unreachable, auto-route to central control cluster in our nominated cloud region.

2) Egress: for ShadowBridge we should require dedicated egress subnets per tenant only if the SOC requirements demand distinct public IP provenance. Otherwise use shared egress with per-tenant SNAT pools and per-flow tagging (we can push tag->tenant mapping to the telemetry) — this saves address space in many colo environments. If ShadowBridge needs strict IP separation for compliance, we can provision dedicated NAT instances in the tenant VLAN.

3) Canary / MOP: I drafted a minimal checklist and attached it (mop-canary-checklist.xlsx). Key items: control-plane cert pin verification, KV cache priming smoke test, tail-latency baseline, and emergency rollback route.

Two operational caveats:
- KV cache warmup requires a brief pre-population window (10–30s) to avoid first-request amplification when traffic is cold. Documented in the checklist.
- If we use shared egress, ensure router rules include strict egress tagging and export to our telemetry collectors for audit.

Happy to review on the sync.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Developer Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ethan/Kim — appreciate the fast turnaround. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Compliance: our security team requires IP-level separation for production (we run regulated data for a financial partner). For the pilot we can accept shared egress provided each pilot tenant is isolated logically and we keep full audit traces, but production will require dedicated NAT.

- Control-plane: regional outbound mTLS to a regional control endpoint is preferred. We also need a documented SLO for how long our agents will attempt regional vs central fallback (we propose 30s then failover).

- KV cache warmup: agree, we will coordinate a priming window during the pilot traffic ramp.

Attached a short note that enumerates the compliance requirement (shadowbridge_compliance_note.pdf). Our SREs can join the sync tomorrow at 10:30 PT if that works.

Regards,

Quick operational check from infra: if production needs dedicated NAT per tenant we should quantify the address and routing impact for the colo sites (some racks are running low on public EIPs). Action items I can own before the sync:
- Run an address inventory for the target colo(s) and estimate cost/complexity for dedicated NAT instances.
- Create a fallback pattern that uses shared egress with per-tenant SNAT as an interim with a documented migration path to dedicated NAT.

Also recommend we include the canary rollback route in the MOP as an automated policy we can flip in the router (not manual).

Marcus
